To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CK 18 is expressed in almost all tumor cells in SCC of the laryngeal and hypopharyngeal mucosa but not in SCC of oral cavity mucosa.

CK 18 staining might be a useful tool in the differential diagnosis of HNSCC, and that the expression pattern of CK 18 in SCCs of the head and the neck might be modulated in the microenvironment of the tumors.
CK 18 is expressed in SCCs of larynx and pharynx but is not expressed in oral cavity SCCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of keratins as tumor markers in SCC of the head and of the neck.
the use of keratin typing in distinguishing between different sites of origin of head and neck SCCs.
the expression of CK in SCCs and the possible use of these proteins in the differential diagnosis of HNSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CK 18 is a useful marker to differentiate between SCCs of the hypopharynx/larynx and SCCs of the mouth.
CK 18 is expressed in the majority of HNSCCs of larynx and pharynx, but not in those arising in the oral cavity.
CK 18 is a marker of laryngohypopharyngeal origin, but that it cannot be used for the identification of the exact subsite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CK 18 staining is a useful tool for distinguishing SCCs of the hypopharynx and larynx from SCC of the oral cavity, but not for distinguishing between the two subsites.
the expression pattern of CK 18 is a useful tool to distinguish between SCCs originating from the larynx/hypopharynx from those arising in the oral cavity.
the CK pattern of HNSCCs is a good indicator of the site of origin of the tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

keratin expression is a good marker of differentiation and that the expression patterns of various keratine subtypes can be used to differentiate between different sites of origin in the head and the neck.
the expression of CK 18 in HNSCCs is useful in distinguishing between SCC of the laryngohypopharyngeal region and SCC of the oral cavity.
CK 18 staining is highly specific to laryngeal squamous cell carcinomata and is therefore of great value in differentiating laryngeal from oral squamous cell carcinomatous lesions.
